request.notes: Lens sends only active filters. Rows live under 'items' — its one and only container key since the first implementation (PR #30's bug was reading invented notes/documents/results aliases). The 'recent'/'recent_tagged' variants are recent_notes' FIRST-page requests: lithos_list has NO ordering parameter (knowledge.list_all returns metadata-cache insertion order; limit/offset slice that order — server-side order_by is upstream Lithos task e0e31654), so the client walks pages of RECENT_NOTES_FETCH_PAGE=500 via 'offset' until the response's 'total' is exhausted, sorting by 'updated' descending itself. Follow-up pages repeat the same shape with offset advanced by the rows received.

observed_divergences: lithos_list has no ordering parameter: items arrive in metadata-cache insertion order (list_all preserves iter_cached_meta order on the full-scan path and restores insertion order via the stored seq on the index path), NOT newest-first. The insertion_ordered_recent variant pins this: its rows are deliberately out of updated-order, and recent_notes must sort them — paginating through the full corpus via offset/total first, so a newly updated note beyond the first page still surfaces. Upstream ordering tracked as Lithos task e0e31654.
